root_cause.text: In the intel/ipu6 PCI probe error path, `ipu6_pci_probe()` treated `isp->psys` as a plain NULL-checked pointer even though it could hold an `ERR_PTR`, causing the cleanup path to dereference an error-encoded pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (isp->psys)` to `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(isp->psys))` in `out_ipu6_bus_del_devices`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that in the error path "`isp->psys` is confirmed to be an error pointer not NULL so this condition is true and the error pointer is dereferenced."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an error-pointer-safe guard in the probe cleanup path to avoid freeing or unmapping an invalid `psys` pointer.
intent_record.what: The null check guarding cleanup in ipu6_pci_probe() was changed from `if (isp->psys)` to `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(isp->psys))` before calling `ipu6_cpd_free_pkg_dir()` and `ipu6_buttress_unmap_fw_image()`.
intent_record.how: This makes the cleanup path skip those teardown calls not only when `isp->psys` is NULL, but also when it contains an error-encoded pointer, preventing invalid dereferences or cleanup on a failed psys initialization result during probe error handling.

grouping_result.intent: Add an error-pointer-safe guard in the probe cleanup path to avoid freeing or unmapping an invalid `psys` pointer.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by making the probe cleanup path handle `isp->psys` as a possible error pointer instead of only NULL-checking it, preventing dereference/free of an `ERR_PTR`.

Author: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Jan 31 17:50:53 2024 +0800

    media: intel/ipu6: add Intel IPU6 PCI device driver
    
    Intel Image Processing Unit 6th Gen includes input and processing systems
    but the hardware presents itself as a single PCI device in system.
    
    The IPU6 PCI device driver basically does PCI configurations and loads the
    firmware binary, initialises IPU virtual bus and sets up platform specif
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible directly in `ipu6_pci_probe()`. `isp->psys` is assigned from `ipu6_psys_init(...)`, and on failure that helper returns an error pointer: `isp->psys = ipu6_psys_init(...); if (IS_ERR(isp->psys)) { ret = PTR_ERR(isp->psys); goto out_ipu6_bus_del_devices; }`. In the shared error path label `out_ipu6_bus_del_devices:`, the code then does `if (isp->psys) { ipu6_cpd_free_pkg_dir(isp->psys); ipu6_buttress_unmap_fw_image(isp->psys, &isp->psys->fw_sgt); }`. This is the root cause described: the code uses a plain truthiness/NULL check (`if (isp->psys)`) even though `isp->psys` may hold an `ERR_PTR`, so cleanup can dereference an error-encoded pointer via `isp->psys->fw_sgt` and pass it to cleanup helpers. Although there is a later guarded check `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(isp->psys) && !IS_ERR_OR_NULL(isp->psys->mmu)) ipu6_mmu_cleanup(isp->psys->mmu);`, that protection is not applied to the earlier cleanup block, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6099f78e4c9223f4de4169d2fd1cded01279da1a
Author: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com>
Date:   Tue Dec 23 15:22:59 2025 +0800

    media: ipu6: Fix RPM reference leak in probe error paths
    
    Several error paths in ipu6_pci_probe() were jumping directly to
    out_ipu6_bus_del_devices without releasing the runtime PM reference.
    Add pm_runtime_put_sync() before cleaning up other resources.
    
    Cc: Stable@vger.kernel.org
    Fixes: 25fedc021985 ("media: intel/ipu6: add Intel IPU6
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it includes the relevant probe error labels and the cleanup check for `isp->psys`. The vulnerability root cause is that `isp->psys` may be an `ERR_PTR`, but the cleanup path treats it as a plain NULL-checked pointer. That vulnerable construct is present here at `out_ipu6_bus_del_devices:` with `if (isp->psys) { ipu6_cpd_free_pkg_dir(isp->psys); ... }`. A non-NULL `ERR_PTR` will satisfy `if (isp->psys)` and then be dereferenced/passed as if valid. The fix for this root cause would require error-pointer-aware handling such as `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(isp->psys))` or equivalent. This commit instead adds `out_ipu6_rpm_put:` and `pm_runtime_put_sync(&isp->psys->auxdev.dev);`, which addresses a runtime PM leak, not the ERR_PTR cleanup bug. In fact, that added line also dereferences `isp->psys` directly and does not show any `IS_ERR` protection. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the ERR_PTR fix is not present.
